page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a cloud server instance within the Cloud Native family, delivering 4 x86_64 vCPUs and 24 GB of system memory. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance runs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz across 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The virtual central processing units utilize shared CPU allocation. No local disk storage is bundled with the instance, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data, and hardware acceleration is absent with a zero GPU count.

Benchmark results show balanced mid-tier computing execution alongside constrained raw throughput. Geekbench scores register 1409.0 in single-core and 5074.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 8197.87 and software compilation performance of 5912.0 points. Conversely, stress-ng benchmarks indicate weaker compute stability under continuous load, recording 780.79 on single-core and 3123.05 on multi-core tests. While cached memory read bandwidth reaches 411.67 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 36.0 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory evaluation shows a lower-tier score of 1246.97.

With 6.0 GB of RAM allocated per core, the configuration offers a generous memory-to-core ratio compared to standard cloud profiles. However, throughput constraints appear across I/O-heavy and intensive services, as demonstrated by Redis processing at 5.87 million operations per second and web serving throughput measuring 3.54 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a 7B parameter model yields 14.28 tokens per second on prompt evaluation and 6.89 tokens per second on text generation.

The shared CPU allocation combined with 24 GB of RAM establishes a cost-effective operational profile for memory-weighted utilities that do not require dedicated core capacity. UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is functionally aligned with staging environments, mid-scale background workers, lightweight application servers, internal continuous integration tasks, and cache-assisted web services.
